subject: science

concepts.title: Combustion
concepts.definition: In brief, a chemical interaction where a material reacts with oxygen to release energy, primarily as heat.
concepts.key_idea: Burning is a chemical process requiring oxygen.
question_patterns: What is combustion?
Define combustible substances.
Is food considered a fuel for the body?
What are the products of burning magnesium?

solution_steps.explain: Check if the substance reacts with oxygen.
Confirm if heat or light is produced during the reaction.

concepts.title: Ignition Temperature
concepts.definition: The minimum temperature threshold that a material must reach to start burning.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, a substance will not catch fire if its temperature is below its ignition point.
question_patterns: What is ignition temperature?
Why does a matchstick not burn on its own at room temperature?
Why do dry leaves catch fire more easily than green leaves?
Explain why paper wrapped around an aluminum pipe does not burn easily.

solution_steps.explain: Determine if the heat source raises the material's temperature to its specific ignition point.

concepts.title: Inflammable Substances
concepts.definition: In brief, Materials that have extremely low ignition both temperatures and can catch fire very easily with a flame.
concepts.key_idea: Substances like LPG and petrol are highly dangerous due to easy ignition.
question_patterns: Define inflammable substances.
Give examples of inflammable materials.
Why are petrol and alcohol called inflammable?

solution_steps.explain: Identify if the substance ignites at very low temperatures.

concepts.title: Fire Control and Extinguishing
concepts.definition: In brief, the method of putting out a fire by removing one or more of the three essential requirements: fuel, air (oxygen), or heat.
concepts.key_idea: Eliminating the supply of oxygen or cooling the fuel stops combustion.
question_patterns: What are the three requirements for producing fire?
How does a fire extinguisher work?
Why is water not used for electrical fires?
How does CO2 control fire?

solution_steps.explain: Determine if the fire involves electricity, oil, or solid combustibles like wood.
Choose water for wood/paper, or CO2 for electrical/oil fires to cut oxygen or lower temperature.

concepts.title: Types of Combustion
concepts.definition: Classification of burning based on speed and initiation, including rapid (fast), spontaneous (untriggered), and explosion (sudden gas release).
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Combustion can occur at different rates and under different conditions.
question_patterns: What is rapid combustion?
Explain spontaneous combustion with an example.
What is an explosion in the context of combustion?
Why do coal mines have spontaneous fires?

solution_steps.explain: Check if the reaction is immediate (rapid) or sudden (explosion).
If it starts without a visible flame/spark, it is spontaneous.

concepts.title: Structure of a Flame
concepts.definition: The physical zones of a flame representing different stages of both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both combustion and temperature levels.
concepts.key_idea: The outer blue zone is the hottest due to complete combustion.
question_patterns: Describe the different zones of a candle flame.
Which is the hottest part of a flame?
Why do goldsmiths use the outermost zone of the flame?
What causes the yellow color in the middle zone?

solution_steps.explain: Locate the outer (blue), middle (yellow), or inner (black) part of the flame.
Outer is complete, middle is partial, inner is unburnt vapours.

concepts.title: Calorific Value
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, the quantity of heat energy formed by the complete burning of exactly one kilogram of a specific fuel.
concepts.key_idea: Higher calorific value indicates a more efficient fuel.
question_patterns: What is calorific value?
Calculate the calorific value if {heat} kJ is produced from {mass} kg of fuel.
In what unit is calorific value expressed?
Which fuel has the highest calorific value?

solution_steps.explain: Calorific value is heat per unit mass.

concepts.title: Environmental Impact of Burning Fuels
concepts.definition: The harmful consequences of fuel combustion, including pollution, global warming, and acid rain.
concepts.key_idea: Incomplete combustion and byproduct gases damage the environment and health.
question_patterns: What are the harmful effects of burning wood?
How is global warming linked to fuel combustion?
What causes acid rain?
Why is CNG called a cleaner fuel?

solution_steps.explain: Check for CO2 (global warming), SO2/NOx (acid rain), or unburnt carbon (respiratory issues).

worked_examples.question_pattern: In an experiment {mass} kg of a fuel was completely burnt. The heat produced was measured to be {heat} kJ. Calculate the calorific value of the fuel.

solution_template.explain: To find the heat per kg, divide the total energy by the total mass.
